The Angle

I have been the enterprise buyer of Gemini, not just a seller against it.

Used Gemini Enterprise extensively, with a heavy focus on NotebookLM, as Salesforce's primary internal AI tool in 2025. That is an unusual vantage point for a candidate on this team: I know what enterprise adoption of this stack actually feels like from the inside of a large, governance-heavy organization, including where it lands and where it stalls.

The second thing I bring is architectural fluency that is not vendor-captive. The four-layer agentic enterprise architecture below is Salesforce's published reference design, not my coinage. What I own is the ability to take it apart and tell a customer which layer Google Cloud occupies, what governance they keep or lose on a swap, and where the open seams sit. In a Canadian enterprise market that is heavily Microsoft and increasingly Databricks, that neutrality is what makes the Google Cloud case credible rather than promotional.

Third: this team reports performance in Salesforce. I know that CRM from twelve years inside it, so the pipeline inspection cadence I would install on day one is not a tooling project.

Architecture

Layers are durable. Vendors inside them are swappable.

Four functional layers, a Trust spine running across all of them, and a model substrate underneath. Every layer carries an open seam by design. Here is where Google Cloud sits in each, and what I bring to the conversation.

Model substrate

Gemini

Used Gemini Enterprise extensively, with a heavy focus on NotebookLM, as Salesforce's primary internal AI tool in 2025. I have been the enterprise buyer and the daily user of the product this team sells, which is a different vantage point than having sold against it.

System of Context

BigQuery, Dataplex, Vertex

Primary Data 360 seller through its major iterations. Positioned Data 360 against Google BigQuery as the central data source at a top Canadian retailer, which meant arguing the data foundation rather than the application. I have run that conversation from the other side of the table.

System of Work

The deliberate open seam

Google partners into SAP, Oracle and Workday rather than owning the workflow layer. Customer 360 multi-cloud deployments at Home Depot Canada, Roots Canada and Harnois Energies are where I learned that adoption is won or lost in the workflow, not the demo.

System of Agency

Vertex AI Agent Builder, Agentspace, A2A

Pre-release agentic AI field evaluator: co-determined with Sales Strategy, Sales Enablement and Sales Programs which generative capabilities, agent frameworks and prompt strategies were enterprise-ready before launch. Google authored A2A, so the interoperability argument is theirs to make.

System of Engagement

Workspace and Gemini Enterprise

The durable law is that the engagement layer accumulates leverage. The specific workspace is the customer's call, and in Canadian enterprise that is as often Microsoft as it is anything else. I built Slack-integrated operations and dashboards without a RevOps function, so I know what the layer is worth when it is wired properly.

Trust spine

Assured Workloads, Sovereign Cloud, residency

Governance runs across all four layers rather than sitting under agents. Demos sell, audits ship. In regulated Canadian retail and financial services, knowing where data and models run is the question that decides the deal.

Operating System

How I would run the team.

About 70% of B2B technology buyers expect to rely more on AI than on sellers, according to IDC, which means they arrive pre-opinionated and gated qualification loses them. The leader's job is system design, not deal heroics.

Methodology sets the language

MEDPICC for deal inspection and Sandler for qualification discipline, run inside a buyer-controlled motion. Forecast calls become evidence-based instead of optimistic.

Coaching changes behaviour

Filling the Funnel and the BASHO framework on every prospecting email and call. Prospecting is a repeatable process, not a mood. Weekly inspection against the gap, not against activity counts.

Competitive plays decide where to attack

In a market of AI sameness, deals default to price or familiarity unless sellers carry a sharp, evidence-based head-to-head story. I competed against Adobe, Oracle, Microsoft, HubSpot, Marketo and Braze in enterprise deals.

The leader wires it into one cadence

Methodology, coaching and competitive intelligence measured on pipeline quality and win rate, delivered in the rep's flow of work rather than in a quarterly workshop that nobody revisits.
